source.title: Some open problems related to stability

accepted.question_text: Consider a stable G/G/m first-come-first-served queue with m > 1 identical servers, stationary ergodic interarrival and service-time sequence {(t_n, sigma_n)}, and initial Kiefer-Wolfowitz workload vector equal to 0. Is the sequence of workload vectors W_n guaranteed to converge in total variation to a stationary distribution pi under only these assumptions, without any additional mixing, independence, regenerativity, or Harris-type conditions? Equivalently, does sup_A |P(W_n in A) - pi(A)| tend to 0 as n goes to infinity for every such stable stationary ergodic input when the process starts from zero workload?

evidence.quote: The conjecture is: assuming only that the sequence {(σ_n, t_n)} is stationary ergodic, that the stability condition holds, and that the initial value is 0, then there is no need for any further restriction to establish the convergence in the total variation: sup_A |P(W_n ∈ A) − π(A)| → 0, n → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Let D be the stationary waiting time in a stable multi-server FCFS queue with i.i.d. service times {sigma_n}, i.i.d. interarrival times {t_n} independent of the service times, and load rho = E sigma_1 / E t_1 < m. When rho is an integer, what are the necessary and sufficient conditions for the power moment E[D^gamma] to be finite for a given gamma > 0?

evidence.quote: An open problem here is: what are the conditions for existence (finiteness) of power moments of D if ρ is an integer.

accepted.question_text: In a two-server FCFS queue with i.i.d. interarrival and service times, stationary waiting time D, and load rho = 1, determine the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large, at least for some concrete subexponential service-time distributions such as regularly varying distributions.

evidence.quote: The open problems here are (I formulate them in the particular case of a two server queue, m = 2): find the asymptotics for P(D > x) (i) if ρ = 1 — at least, for some particular subexponential (say, regularly varying) distribution of service times;

accepted.question_text: In a two-server FCFS queue with i.i.d. interarrival and service times, stationary waiting time D, and load rho in (1, 2), determine the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large when the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed but still has all power moments finite, for example when P(sigma_1 > x) = exp(-x^beta) with beta in (0, 1).

evidence.quote: (ii) if ρ ∈ (1, 2) and if the distribution of service times is heavy-tailed but has all power moments finite, for example, if P(σ_1 > x) = e^{-x^β}, for some β ∈ (0, 1).

accepted.question_text: For the rare-event regimes described for the two-server FCFS queue, identify the typical sample paths in the past input and service process that produce unusually large values of the stationary waiting time D.

evidence.quote: It would be great to understand what are in these cases the “typical” paths which lead to large values of D.

accepted.question_text: Consider a stable multi-server queue, for example a two-server system, with stationary ergodic input {(t_n, sigma_n)} and the join-the-shortest-queue discipline, where each arrival immediately joins one of the shortest individual queues. Under only the obvious stability condition and no additional assumptions, how many stationary regimes can this system have?

evidence.quote: So, here are the open problems: — how many stationary regimes may exist if we do not assume any extra condition in addition to the obvious stability condition?

accepted.question_text: For the stationary ergodic join-the-shortest-queue multi-server model, what are the weakest additional assumptions that guarantee uniqueness of the stationary regime?

evidence.quote: — what are the minimal requirements for the uniqueness of the stationary regime?

accepted.question_text: For the join-the-shortest-queue multi-server system with stationary ergodic input, under what assumptions, possibly none beyond stability, does the process converge weakly or in total variation to a stationary regime?

evidence.quote: — under what conditions (none?) do we have weak (or TV) convergence?

accepted.question_text: A server moves on a circle. Particles arrive according to a Poisson process of rate lambda, each particle requires one unit of service time, and after every service completion the server travels at positive finite constant speed to the nearest waiting particle, ignoring new arrivals while moving. Is this greedy-server system stable for every lambda < 1?

evidence.quote: The conjecture is: this model is stable for any λ < 1.

accepted.question_text: On a circle, black particles arrive as a Poisson rain of rate lambda and remain until deleted, while white particles arrive independently at rate 1, immediately disappear, and each white particle deletes the nearest black particle within a fixed epsilon-neighborhood if one exists. Is this system stable whenever lambda < 1, independently of the circle length and of epsilon?

evidence.quote: The natural conjecture is: stability should be guaranteed by the condition λ < 1, independently of the circle length and the number ε. But the problem is open too.

accepted.question_text: Do there exist simple queueing systems for which stability depends not only on the usual load-type parameters but also on the initial state and on the full distribution of the driving sequences? In particular, can one rigorously prove this phenomenon for the three-server, three-customer-class routing model described here, where each arriving customer joins the accessible server with the shorter workload and the service-time law depends on whether the chosen server is the left or right accessible server?

evidence.quote: The conjecture is: even in simple queueing systems, the stability conditions may depend both on the initial values and on the whole distribution of the driving sequences.
Simulations show that the conjecture may hold, but there is no a rigorous proof.

accepted.question_text: Consider the open polling system with two stations and two heterogeneous servers, Poisson input rate 1 at each station, exponential service rates mu_i^(j) for server j at station i, exhaustive service, and zero switchover time. Inside the positive four-dimensional parameter cube for {mu_i^(j)}, does the subset of parameter values for which the system is null recurrent have positive Lebesgue measure?

evidence.quote: The conjecture here is: in the positive 4-dimensional cube, the set of parameters {µ_i^(j)} for which the system is “null-recurrent” has a positive Lebesgue measure.

accepted.question_text: In the slotted multi-access channel where a Poisson(lambda) number of packets arrive each slot, every packet transmits in slot n with common probability p_n, collisions keep packets in the system, successful solo transmissions remove a packet, and p_{n+1} may depend only on p_n and the binary information of whether slot n contained a successful transmission, does there exist a protocol that makes the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) positive recurrent for some lambda > 0?

evidence.quote: The open question is: in the class of procedures (protocols) described above, does there exist a protocol which makes the Markov chain (W_n, p_n) positive recurrent (ergodic), for some positive λ?
